renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: fdr_profile
  title: Accepted PSMs against FDR
  description: |-
    Each curve is a raw file: the number of target peptide-spectrum matches (PSMs) accepted as the target-decoy q-value threshold on the raw Comet score is relaxed. It answers how many identifications each file yields at a given error rate.
    How to read: a curve that rises steeply and early belongs to a file with good spectra, while a flat curve has few confident matches and points to an acquisition or search-space problem. Compare files: one far below its peers is the one to investigate.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical marker is the 1% false discovery rate, the nf-core/mhcquant default fdr_threshold at which peptide hits are selected. This curve applies it to target-decoy competition on the raw Comet score, from the table the pipeline hands to its rescoring engine (Percolator by default). Its counts therefore differ from the final peptide table, which is rescored and filtered at peptide level by default.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/mhcquant/master/nextflow_schema.json and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17327847/
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Target-decoy q-value
    y_title: Accepted target PSMs
    reference_x: 0.01
    reference_label: 1% FDR
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: run_id
    x: q_value
    y: accepted_psms

- component: figure
  title: Accepted PSMs by FDR threshold
  description: |-
    Each line is a raw file: the accepted target PSMs at each q-value threshold. It answers how the files compare across the whole 0 to 10% range, not only at one cut-off.
    How to read: lines that run in parallel differ in depth but not in quality. Lines that cross differ in how their score distributions separate targets from decoys.
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: q_value
    y: accepted_psms
    color: run_id
    labels:
      q_value: Target-decoy q-value
      accepted_psms: Accepted target PSMs
      run_id: Raw file

- component: table
  title: Accepted PSMs per threshold
  description: |-
    Each row is a threshold on one raw file: the q-value, the number of accepted target PSMs and the Comet score cut-off that gives it. It answers which score cut-off corresponds to a given error rate.
    How to read: pick the row nearest the error rate you report at and read its score cut-off.

outputs.name: Comet search yield per raw file

renders._yaml:
- component: card
  title: PSMs at 1% FDR
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of target PSMs accepted at a 1% target-decoy false discovery rate on the raw Comet score, with the spread across raw files in the box. It answers how productive the search is before rescoring.
    How to read: a tight box means files of similar yield. A file far below the others has an acquisition or search-space problem rather than a rescoring one.
    Note: the 1% is the nf-core/mhcquant default fdr_threshold, applied here by this module to the raw Comet score rather than after rescoring.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/mhcquant/master/nextflow_schema.json
  column: psms_1pct_fdr
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with the spread

- component: card
  title: Identification rate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of searched spectra that give a target PSM passing the filter, as a fraction between 0 and 1, with the spread across raw files in the box. It answers how efficiently the acquired spectra are explained.
    How to read: a low rate with many spectra searched points to noisy spectra or a search space that does not fit the sample. Search engines publish no universal cut-off for this rate.
  column: identification_rate
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with the spread

- component: card
  title: Precursor mass error
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median precursor mass error in parts per million across raw files, with the spread in the box. It answers whether the instrument is calibrated.
    How to read: values close to zero with a tight spread mean good calibration. A file shifted away from the others needs recalibration or a wider search tolerance.
  column: median_mass_error_ppm
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with the spread

- component: advanced_viz
  id: target_decoy_separation
  title: Target and decoy score separation
  description: |-
    Each point is a raw file: the median Comet score of its decoy matches (horizontal) against that of its target matches (vertical), sized by the number of spectra searched. It answers how well the search separates real matches from random ones.
    How to read: points well above the diagonal have target scores clearly higher than decoy scores, which is what a good search looks like. A point near the diagonal has a search that cannot tell targets from decoys, so its identifications are unreliable.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is y = x, where target and decoy scores are equal, a reference defined by the plot and not a tool cut-off. The target-decoy strategy it rests on is described in the source.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17327847/
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Median decoy Xcorr
    y_title: Median target Xcorr
    reference_line: diagonal
    reference_label: Target = decoy
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    x: median_xcorr_decoy
    y: median_xcorr_target
    label: run_id
    size: spectra_searched
    color: run_id

- component: table
  title: Search yield per raw file
  description: |-
    Each row is a raw file: spectra searched, target and decoy PSMs, the PSMs accepted at 1% and 5% FDR, the identification rate, the median scores, the mass error and the peptide length. It answers which files to look at first.
    How to read: sort by the 1% FDR count to rank the files, then click a row to filter the other tiles to that file.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: run_id
